```{r}
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, palmerpenguins)
```

## The question

**Are there differences?**

One continuous variable, such as the weight, across groups, such as the species.

---

# 1. The boxplot {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**geom_boxplot()**

---

## Box default

```{r}
#| message: true
#| warning: true
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

`Removed 2 rows`: 2 penguins have no body mass. `filter(!is.na(body_mass_g))` removes them.

---

## Box

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

The line in the box is the median. The box holds the middle half of the penguins. The whiskers reach the rest, and a dot marks a value far from the box. Medians: Adelie 3,700 g, Chinstrap 3,700 g, Gentoo 5,000 g.

---

# 2. The box hides the shape {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**geom_jitter()**

---

## Box point

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point()
```

The boxes of Adelie and Chinstrap look alike: both medians are 3,700 g, and the boxes run from 3,350 to 4,000 g and from 3,488 to 3,950 g. Let us add each penguin as a point.

Every point of a species sits on one vertical line, so we cannot count them.

---

## Box jitter

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2)
```

`geom_jitter()` moves each point a random distance sideways. The horizontal position has no meaning. The vertical position is still the real weight. `width = 0.2` sets how far a point can move.

---

# 3. The violin {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**geom_violin()**

---

## Violin

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_violin()
```

The violin is wide where many penguins have that weight. Gentoo shows two bumps, and the box of Gentoo hid them. Chinstrap has one symmetric bump, and Adelie is wider at the top.

---

# 4. All together {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Layers**

---

## Together

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.3)
```

ggplot draws the layers in the order we add them, so the violin goes first. `width = 0.1` makes the box narrow. `alpha = 0.3` makes the points see-through.

---

# 5. Why two bumps? (optional) {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Optional**

---

## Sex na

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = sex), width = 0.1)
```

Color the jittered points by sex. A grey group appears: 11 penguins have no sex.

`filter(!is.na(sex))` removes the grey group.

---

## Sex

```{r}
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g), !is.na(sex)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = sex), width = 0.1)
```

The two bumps of Gentoo are the two sexes. Females average 4,680 g and males average 5,485 g.

---

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| Median and spread of each group | `geom_boxplot()` |
| Each penguin as a point | `geom_jitter(width = 0.2)` |
| Shape of the distribution | `geom_violin()` |
| Narrow box | `geom_boxplot(width = 0.1)` |
| See-through points | `alpha = 0.3` |
| Color the points by a variable | `geom_jitter(aes(color = sex))` |
